label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Handover for Thursday's launch (Inês, please read first)

Inês,

I'm sorry to drop this on you. My father is ill and I'm with my family in the Netherlands. I'm taking the train tonight and I don't know yet how long I'll be away, so you'll be doing Thursday without me.

Before the to-do list, two things I want you to hear from me.

First, I trust you completely with this. You know the paper as well as I do, and you know annex B better than I do because you ran the sensitivity runs yourself. Remember Lisbon, when the projector died halfway through my panel at the COP side event? You were the one who kept the room together, not me. You are better live than you think. There's nobody I'd rather hand this to.

Second, I'm sorry about the state I'm leaving it in. I only found the error in figure 3 this afternoon. The 2.1 billion was my mistake, not yours. If anyone asks, journalists, Lindqvist's office, Kessler, anyone, please say so plainly: "Marieke used an estimate from an earlier run; the corrected figure is 1.4 billion." You don't need to protect me, and it's true.

Everything below is in the launch folder or my inbox. I've put it in the order I'd do it.

1. THE CORRECTION (do this first, Tuesday morning if you can)

What's wrong: figure 3 and the summary used the 2030 revenue estimate from the old run, before the free allocation phase-out was applied. The correct 2030 LDC-relevant revenue is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion. The conclusion of the paper doesn't change, but the headline number does. My note "ERROR figure 3 - must fix before launch" in the folder has the details.

Already fixed: PDF v7 on the drive (pages 3, 14 and 15). Please make sure v7 is the version that goes on the website and gets printed, and that nobody picks up v6 by accident. If you have ten minutes, give v7 one more read for any other stray 2.1. I fixed the pages I found, but I was in a hurry.

Not fixed yet:

a) The press release. This is the urgent one. Hanna sent it on Friday to our 34 Brussels contacts, embargoed until Thursday 26 November 10:00 CET, and it says 2.1. It has to be corrected and resent well before the embargo lifts. Ideally Tuesday, Wednesday morning at the latest, so journalists don't write it up with the wrong number. Please sit down with Hanna and agree a short corrected release with a clear line at the top (something like "Correction: the 2030 estimate is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion as in the version sent on 20 November"). Keep it factual and don't over-apologise. If Hanna wants a senior name to sign it off, ask Geert. He knows I'm away and he's said he can do it.

b) The deck. Deck v4, slides 6 and 9 still show 2.1 (slide 9 is the revenue chart). Update the number and the chart from the v7 figure, and check my speaker notes too because I'm fairly sure I wrote 2.1 in there as well.

2. BADGES: deadline Wednesday 12:00

Tomás (Lindqvist's office) needs the final names of everyone coming from our side by Wednesday 12:00 at the latest, or security won't let them in. Please send him the list. It should have you instead of me, plus Hanna and anyone else from the institute who's coming. Don't leave this until Wednesday morning. Guests have to be at the security entrance by 12:00 on Thursday and Tomás collects the badges.

3. TELL TOMÁS AND ACCEPT THE NEW TIMINGS

Tomás wrote this morning (it's in my inbox, "Thursday - small change to timings"). Lindqvist has a vote moved into Thursday lunchtime and has to leave at 13:30. He asked whether the presentation can be 15 minutes instead of 20 and the panel can start at 12:50. She also wants to take at least two questions herself before she goes.

I haven't replied. Please reply when you send the badge names. Say yes to the new timings, and tell him you'll be presenting and sitting on the panel instead of me. You don't need to explain beyond "Marieke has a family emergency". You can also give him the heads-up about the corrected figure so Lindqvist doesn't quote 2.1 in her welcome. That one matters, actually. She may have read the press release.

New running order as I understand it:
- 12:00 guests at security, lunch outside the room
- 12:30 welcome, Lindqvist (5 min)
- 12:35 your presentation (15 min)
- 12:50 panel: Abena (remote), Kessler, you. Lindqvist moderates
- Lindqvist takes at least two questions before 13:30, then leaves
- Q&A until 14:00, close

Check with Tomás who moderates after 13:30. Probably you, unless he has someone from the office in mind. If it's you, that's fine. Just keep it moving and close on time.

4. THE TALK

Cutting from 20 to 15 minutes is easier than it sounds. The deck is already down to 14 slides. I'd keep the problem, the revenue estimate with the correct number, what it means for the LDCs, and the recommendations, and go lightly over the method. Say the corrected number early and once, clearly, and then move on. If you state it confidently it becomes a non-event. Use my speaker notes if they help, but say it your way.

5. PRESS CALLS: Wednesday 14:00 and 15:00

Two journalists asked for background calls before the event, one from a trade newsletter and one from a Belgian daily. Hanna told them I'd be available Wednesday afternoon, and the calendar has 14:00 and 15:00, 20 minutes each, by phone. Please ask Hanna to confirm with both of them that you'll take the calls instead. By then they should have the corrected release. If they ask about the change, see above: earlier run, my mistake, conclusion unchanged.

6. KESSLER

Florian Kessler (Alliance of European Steel Users) will try to make the whole panel about the 80% pass-through assumption. His written comments are in the folder. Please don't let him set the tone. Acknowledge the point, answer it once, and bring it back to the LDCs, which is what the paper is about.

My reply lines (also in the folder, "Reply lines for Kessler"):
- 80% is the central case. Annex B runs 40% and 60%. The result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%. Say this openly and don't get defensive. You ran those numbers, so nobody in that room knows them better than you.
- Resource shuffling: we agree it's a risk, it's covered in section 5.2, and we recommend the Commission's monitoring report.
- Abena will probably back us on the LDC side. She was strong on our call. Bring her in early so it isn't you against him.

7. ABENA (REMOTE)

The link is in the calendar invite and you said she tested it last week and it worked. I'd still ask Tomás or the room technician to do a quick sound check with her before 12:30 on Thursday. Lisbon taught us both that lesson.

8. AFTER THE EVENT

Lucy Tran from the Halvorsen Foundation is coming with a colleague. For their grant report they need two photos from the event and the attendance numbers, ideally by 4 December. Could you ask Hanna or someone to take photos (the panel, and one with the room), and get a headcount from Tomás or the sign-in list? Lucy also congratulated both of us on finishing the paper. Please say hello to her for me, and thank her for coming.

9. REACHING ME

You can call me. Tomorrow (Tuesday) before 9 in the morning is the best time. After that I might not pick up, so if I don't answer, leave a message or text me and I'll get back to you when I can. For anything that needs a decision and can't wait for me, go to Geert. And for the small stuff, honestly, just decide. Your judgement is good.

Quick checklist:
[ ] Corrected press release agreed with Hanna, signed off by Geert if needed, resent before Thursday 10:00
[ ] PDF v7 confirmed as the live and printed version
[ ] Deck v4 slides 6 and 9 and speaker notes corrected to 1.4
[ ] Badge names to Tomás by Wednesday 12:00
[ ] Reply to Tomás: new timings OK, you're presenting, flag the corrected number for Lindqvist
[ ] Hanna confirms the Wednesday 14:00 and 15:00 press calls with you
[ ] Sound check with Abena on Thursday
[ ] Photos and attendance numbers to Lucy by 4 December

That's everything I can think of. Thank you, Inês. I mean it. I'm sorry I won't be in the room, and I know it'll go well.

Marieke

reasons: The handover includes the Netherlands and train journey beyond the permitted family basics.
